reasons: Section 14(a) applies Delaware law, which is expressly an accepted fallback jurisdiction under GOVLAW, with exclusive venue in the state and federal courts of New York, New York — the preferred forum; the deterministic check confirms the governing law sits within the accepted set.

Section 8's AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules clause is a domestic US forum with no foreign seat, so the walk-away trigger (vendor home jurisdiction outside the accepted list or arbitration seated abroad) is not engaged.

Per the classification semantics, a clause meeting the fallback on its material terms is compliant and should not be redlined; the rationale correctly notes the Delaware-vs-New York point and the Section 8/14(a) forum tension as minor observations rather than deviations.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no counterparty comment was generated.
